facts.text: New Mexico State Road 116 passes through Pueblitos, connecting the community to surrounding areas.
The name 'Pueblitos'—Spanish for 'small villages'—derives from the modest Native American ruins that dot the landscape.
Archaeologists have identified roughly 100 pueblito sites in the area, hinting at many more yet to be discovered.
These ruins sit atop steep mesas, overlooking canyons and streams, offering defenders a clear view of approaching enemies.
Proximity to the Rio Grande River supports irrigated agriculture in Pueblitos, but low-lying zones risk flooding during heavy monsoon rains.
Pueblitos maintains a rural character typical of Valencia County's unincorporated areas, with low-density residential zoning and agriculture preserving the historic greenbelt along the river.
